description: An agent-bank notice telling a lender that a borrowing (drawdown) has occurred or will occur on a facility, stating the lender's share of the new advance alongside the facility-wide total. Look for a drawdown or borrowing activity label, a new-contract or current-contract block with rate components, and an unfunded commitment before/after pair. Distinguish from a paydown notice by direction: a borrowing increases the outstanding balance. IMPORTANT: many agent banks print these on a template titled `Activity Memo` with the real activity named in a banner line below it, such as `*** Prime Borrowing ***` or `*** LIBOR Drawdown ***`. Classify by the banner, not the template title -- a document headed `Activity Memo` that announces a borrowing on a single facility is a `borrowing_notice`, not an `activity_memo`.

activity_type.description: The source document's OWN word for what it reports, copied as printed rather than mapped to a standard vocabulary: `Prime Borrowing`, `Commitment Fee`, `Interest`, `Rollover`, `Mandatory Paydown`. Usually the activity or transaction-type label, or the notice's own title. Give the ACTIVITY ALONE: strip any leading interest-rate option, tenor or currency the label is prefixed with, because those describe pricing rather than activity -- a description reading `Term SOFR 3 Month Principal Payment` yields `Principal Payment`, and `USD Loan Repricing for the Deal X/Decrease` yields `Repricing`. Never include a deal name, facility name or amount here.

agent_bank.description: The institution SENDING the notice -- the administrative agent, on the letterhead or in the `From:` block. Not the borrower and not the recipient fund. Copy as printed, including the legal suffix.

agent_contact_name.description: The named person or desk at the AGENT BANK -- the sender's contact, in the letterhead, signature block, footer or a `Contact:` line (`Delia Cranmore`, `AGENCY SERVICES`). A team or desk name is a valid value where no individual is named. LOOK AT THE BOTTOM OF THE PAGE FIRST: these notices carry the agent's contact on a `Contact:` line or in a closing block after the figures, frequently as initial and surname (`T. OKAFOR`, `MICHAEL REED`). Prefer that over the `ATTN:` line of the recipient's address block, which names the fund's own staff (`PORTFOLIO ADMIN`, `Fee Administration`) rather than the sender's -- but where `ATTN:` holds the only personal name on the page, use it rather than leaving the field empty.

agent_email.description: The agent bank's contact email address, verbatim, with the printed capitalisation kept as-is. Do not invent a domain. This is often in a mail header at the very top of the page rather than in a contact block -- `Mail Sent From:`, `Message Originated From:`, `From:` and `Sender:` lines all carry it, and all count: take it. A `Contact:` line further down that pairs a name with an address is equally valid. Only omit the key when the page shows no email address at all.

agent_telephone.description: The agent bank's contact telephone number, exactly as printed including any country code, spaces, dots or dashes (`212-555-0100`, `+1-555-0177`).

amount.description: The FUND-ATTRIBUTABLE amount only -- the recipient's share. Agent notices print a facility-wide total and the recipient's share side by side, typically labelled `Global Amount` and `Your Share`; this field is `Your Share`. If the document prints ONLY a facility-wide total and no recipient share, OMIT this key entirely and put the total in `global_amount` -- do not fall back to the global figure here. Emitting a facility-wide total as `amount` makes the reconciliation compare the wrong two numbers. Emit as a plain decimal number with no thousands separators, no currency symbol and no parentheses: `67,900.00` becomes `67900.00`.

counterparty.description: The borrower or issuer the notice is about -- the obligor named on the deal, NOT the fund receiving the notice and NOT the agent bank sending it. Usually printed against a label such as `Borrower:`, `Issuer:` or `Deal:`. Copy the name as printed, including its legal suffix. Together with `notice_date` this is the platform's index key, so it matters more than any other field on the page.

currency.description: The ISO 4217 three-letter code for the currency the amounts are denominated in (`USD`, `EUR`). Convert a symbol or a spelled-out name to the code.

facility.description: The credit facility or tranche the notice concerns, as named on the document (`2023 Delayed Draw`, `USD 450M Revolving Credit Facility`, `TERM LOAN A`, `INITIAL TERM LOANS`). The descriptive name, not the id -- the id goes in `facility_id_source_raw`. NOT the interest-rate option: `Term SOFR 3 Month`, `Base Rate`, `LIBOR 1 Month` and `Prime` name how the loan is priced, not which facility it is, and a notice normally prints both. The facility is the loan itself -- a term loan, revolver or delayed-draw tranche -- and is often on the `Re:` or `Deal:` line after the borrower name rather than on the description or rate line.

fund.description: The fund or portfolio the notice concerns -- the lender side, as distinct from `counterparty`, which is the borrower. PREFER AN EXPLICITLY LABELLED VALUE: when the document carries a `Portfolio:`, `Fund:`, `Lender:` or `Investor:` label, take that value verbatim, even where it is a short internal name (`Senior Credit Fund`, `DL Fund II`) and a longer legal entity is named elsewhere on the page. Only when no such label exists fall back to the addressee on the `TO:` line or in the address block. The labelled value is the one the platform holds; the addressee is often the same fund's registered legal name (`HARBORLIGHT SENIOR LOAN FUND LP`) and does not match. Never a servicing platform, vendor or software name.

global_amount.description: The facility-wide total, typically labelled `Global Amount`, `Global Prime Borrowing` or `Total Facility Amount`. Never the recipient's share -- that is `amount`. Emit as a plain decimal number with no thousands separators, no currency symbol and no parentheses: `67,900.00` becomes `67900.00`.

notice_comment.description: Free-text remarks, notes or comments the notice carries, gathered into one string in document order. Includes the producing office, run-date footers and any explanatory paragraph. Emit an empty string when the document has a remarks area that is blank; omit the key when it has no remarks area at all.

notice_date.description: The date the agent bank issued this notice, as printed on the document. Normalise to ISO 8601 `YYYY-MM-DD` regardless of how the document prints it (`2/2/2026`, `02-Feb-2026` and `February 2, 2026` all become `2026-02-02`). This field and `counterparty` are the two the reconciliation platform indexes on; prioritise them above everything else. If the document prints only an effective or value date and no issue date, leave this absent and populate `value_date`.

notice_date_source_raw.description: The notice date exactly as printed on the document, before any normalisation, including its original separators and month spelling (`2/2/2026`, `17-Nov-2026`). Copy the characters verbatim; do not reformat, reorder or expand them.

value_date.description: The date the cash actually moves or the rate takes effect -- the document's effective date, settlement date or payment date. Normalise to ISO 8601 `YYYY-MM-DD` regardless of how the document prints it (`2/2/2026`, `02-Feb-2026` and `February 2, 2026` all become `2026-02-02`). Often equal to `notice_date`; emit both when both are printed, because the platform falls back to this one.

description: An agent-bank notice that both sets a new interest rate AND reports an interest payment on the same document -- rate components (base rate, spread, all-in rate) together with a cash interest amount due. A banner reading `****** Interest Payment ******` puts the document here even when the amount columns show only a facility-wide `Global Amount` and no `Your Share`: a missing share column means the share was not disclosed, not that no payment was made. Likewise, the word `Rollover` appearing inside a rate description (`Term SOFR Rollover Interest`) names the rate basis, not the document type -- it does not make this a rollover notice.

activity_type.description: The source document's OWN word for what it reports, copied as printed rather than mapped to a standard vocabulary: `Prime Borrowing`, `Commitment Fee`, `Interest`, `Rollover`, `Mandatory Paydown`. Usually the activity or transaction-type label, or the notice's own title. Give the ACTIVITY ALONE: strip any leading interest-rate option, tenor or currency the label is prefixed with, because those describe pricing rather than activity -- a description reading `Term SOFR 3 Month Principal Payment` yields `Principal Payment`, and `USD Loan Repricing for the Deal X/Decrease` yields `Repricing`. Never include a deal name, facility name or amount here.

agent_bank.description: The institution SENDING the notice -- the administrative agent, on the letterhead or in the `From:` block. Not the borrower and not the recipient fund. Copy as printed, including the legal suffix.

agent_email.description: The agent bank's contact email address, verbatim, with the printed capitalisation kept as-is. Do not invent a domain. This is often in a mail header at the very top of the page rather than in a contact block -- `Mail Sent From:`, `Message Originated From:`, `From:` and `Sender:` lines all carry it, and all count: take it. A `Contact:` line further down that pairs a name with an address is equally valid. Only omit the key when the page shows no email address at all.

agent_telephone.description: The agent bank's contact telephone number, exactly as printed including any country code, spaces, dots or dashes (`212-555-0100`, `+1-555-0177`).

amount.description: The FUND-ATTRIBUTABLE amount only -- the recipient's share. Agent notices print a facility-wide total and the recipient's share side by side, typically labelled `Global Amount` and `Your Share`; this field is `Your Share`. If the document prints ONLY a facility-wide total and no recipient share, OMIT this key entirely and put the total in `global_amount` -- do not fall back to the global figure here. Emitting a facility-wide total as `amount` makes the reconciliation compare the wrong two numbers. Emit as a plain decimal number with no thousands separators, no currency symbol and no parentheses: `67,900.00` becomes `67900.00`.

counterparty.description: The borrower or issuer the notice is about -- the obligor named on the deal, NOT the fund receiving the notice and NOT the agent bank sending it. Usually printed against a label such as `Borrower:`, `Issuer:` or `Deal:`. Copy the name as printed, including its legal suffix. Together with `notice_date` this is the platform's index key, so it matters more than any other field on the page.

currency.description: The ISO 4217 three-letter code for the currency the amounts are denominated in (`USD`, `EUR`). Convert a symbol or a spelled-out name to the code.

facility.description: The credit facility or tranche the notice concerns, as named on the document (`2023 Delayed Draw`, `USD 450M Revolving Credit Facility`, `TERM LOAN A`, `INITIAL TERM LOANS`). The descriptive name, not the id -- the id goes in `facility_id_source_raw`. NOT the interest-rate option: `Term SOFR 3 Month`, `Base Rate`, `LIBOR 1 Month` and `Prime` name how the loan is priced, not which facility it is, and a notice normally prints both. The facility is the loan itself -- a term loan, revolver or delayed-draw tranche -- and is often on the `Re:` or `Deal:` line after the borrower name rather than on the description or rate line.

fund.description: The fund or portfolio the notice concerns -- the lender side, as distinct from `counterparty`, which is the borrower. PREFER AN EXPLICITLY LABELLED VALUE: when the document carries a `Portfolio:`, `Fund:`, `Lender:` or `Investor:` label, take that value verbatim, even where it is a short internal name (`Senior Credit Fund`, `DL Fund II`) and a longer legal entity is named elsewhere on the page. Only when no such label exists fall back to the addressee on the `TO:` line or in the address block. The labelled value is the one the platform holds; the addressee is often the same fund's registered legal name (`HARBORLIGHT SENIOR LOAN FUND LP`) and does not match. Never a servicing platform, vendor or software name.

global_amount.description: The facility-wide total, typically labelled `Global Amount`, `Global Prime Borrowing` or `Total Facility Amount`. Never the recipient's share -- that is `amount`. Emit as a plain decimal number with no thousands separators, no currency symbol and no parentheses: `67,900.00` becomes `67900.00`.

notice_date.description: The date the agent bank issued this notice, as printed on the document. Normalise to ISO 8601 `YYYY-MM-DD` regardless of how the document prints it (`2/2/2026`, `02-Feb-2026` and `February 2, 2026` all become `2026-02-02`). This field and `counterparty` are the two the reconciliation platform indexes on; prioritise them above everything else. If the document prints only an effective or value date and no issue date, leave this absent and populate `value_date`.

notice_date_source_raw.description: The notice date exactly as printed on the document, before any normalisation, including its original separators and month spelling (`2/2/2026`, `17-Nov-2026`). Copy the characters verbatim; do not reformat, reorder or expand them.

value_date.description: The date the cash actually moves or the rate takes effect -- the document's effective date, settlement date or payment date. Normalise to ISO 8601 `YYYY-MM-DD` regardless of how the document prints it (`2/2/2026`, `02-Feb-2026` and `February 2, 2026` all become `2026-02-02`). Often equal to `notice_date`; emit both when both are printed, because the platform falls back to this one.

description: A document that arrived truncated, illegible or incomplete -- a partial fax, a bare cover sheet, a scan missing pages. Classify a document here rather than guessing the class it would have been: a wrong class with confident fields is worse than an honest incomplete. Recognisable by a cover sheet with no substantive body, a page-count line the document does not satisfy, or a body cut off mid-table. Extract only the few fields actually legible.

agent_contact_name.description: The named person or desk at the AGENT BANK -- the sender's contact, in the letterhead, signature block, footer or a `Contact:` line (`Delia Cranmore`, `AGENCY SERVICES`). A team or desk name is a valid value where no individual is named. LOOK AT THE BOTTOM OF THE PAGE FIRST: these notices carry the agent's contact on a `Contact:` line or in a closing block after the figures, frequently as initial and surname (`T. OKAFOR`, `MICHAEL REED`). Prefer that over the `ATTN:` line of the recipient's address block, which names the fund's own staff (`PORTFOLIO ADMIN`, `Fee Administration`) rather than the sender's -- but where `ATTN:` holds the only personal name on the page, use it rather than leaving the field empty.
